day-57-act-01.title: Corrupted, Truncated and Incompatible Checkpoint Diagnosis
day-57-act-01.prerequisites: Day 55 Checkpoints and error handling mechanics.
day-57-act-01.objective: Diagnose partial-write truncations (EOFError, pickle UnpicklingError), verify SHA256 checksums, and automate fallback to the most recent healthy historical checkpoint.
day-57-act-01.instructions:
1. Understand failure modes when processes are killed during standard write operations: file size is non-zero, but end of file is truncated.
2. Attempting to torch.load a truncated checkpoint throws _pickle.UnpicklingError: pickle data was truncated or EOFError.
3. Implement a checksum verification protocol: along with 'ckpt.pt', save 'ckpt.pt.sha256'. Verify hashes before loading.
4. Build an automated multi-stage fallback: if checkpoint_step_10000 fails validation, seamlessly fall back to checkpoint_step_9000 and notify the training supervisor.
day-57-act-01.exercise_prompt: Write a recovery loader safe_load_checkpoint(checkpoint_dir) that iterates backwards through sorted checkpoint snapshots, rejects corrupted or truncated files, and successfully loads the latest valid state.
day-57-act-01.hint: Iterate snapshots in reverse sorted order (sorted(files, reverse=True)). If a .sha256 file exists, verify the hash first; then wrap torch.load in try/except (EOFError, RuntimeError, Exception) and skip any file that fails.
day-57-act-01.mastery_criterion: Demonstrate automatic fallback to an intact historical snapshot when the newest snapshot is intentionally truncated.

day-57-act-02.title: Partial Weight Loading, Vocabulary Expansions & Strict Mode Management
day-57-act-02.prerequisites: Day 57 Activity 1, PyTorch module parameter dictionaries.
day-57-act-02.objective: Perform partial weight transfers across altered architectures using strict=False, safely expand embedding layers for new tokens, and audit missing_keys vs unexpected_keys.
day-57-act-02.instructions:
1. Understand load_state_dict(..., strict=False) return values: incompatible_keys has missing_keys and unexpected_keys attributes.
2. Handle vocabulary expansion: when fine-tuning a model on a new domain with added special tokens, vocab_size changes from V_old to V_new.
3. Transfer old embeddings: copy existing weights into the new [V_new, d] tensor and initialize new token embeddings with small random gaussian noise or mean embedding.
4. Avoid common silent bugs: verify that missing keys are only the newly added modules, not accidentally misspelled layer names.
day-57-act-02.exercise_prompt: Take a pretrained model with vocab_size=100. Expand the vocabulary to 105. Safely load the old weights with strict=False, initialize the 5 new token embeddings, and verify the old 100 token outputs remain completely unaltered.
day-57-act-02.hint: model.transformer.wte.weight.data[:100] = old_wte.data; verify torch.equal on existing tokens.
day-57-act-02.answer:
new_wte = torch.nn.Embedding(105, 64)
with torch.no_grad():
    new_wte.weight[:100] = old_wte.weight
    new_wte.weight[100:].normal_(mean=0.0, std=0.02)
assert torch.equal(new_wte.weight[:100], old_wte.weight)
day-57-act-02.mastery_criterion: Successfully expand model vocab without altering existing token representations.

day-57-act-03.title: Cloud Spot Preemption Signals, Graceful SIGTERM Handling & Billing Safeguards
day-57-act-03.prerequisites: Day 57 Activity 1, Linux POSIX signals and cloud spot economics.
day-57-act-03.objective: Register Python signal handlers for SIGTERM/SIGINT to immediately trigger emergency atomic checkpoint persistence when a cloud Spot GPU node receives preemption notice, protecting research budgets from lost progress.
day-57-act-03.instructions:
1. Understand cloud spot instances: cloud providers offer up to 70-90% discounts on preemptible GPUs, but issue a termination notice (typically 30 to 120 seconds notice) via SIGTERM or metadata service.
2. In Python, import signal and register signal.signal(signal.SIGTERM, sigterm_handler).
3. In the handler, set a global flag graceful_exit = True. At the end of the current training step, flush an emergency atomic checkpoint and exit cleanly with code 0.
4. Analyze disk I/O cost trade-offs: checkpointing every step destroys GPU throughput due to disk write latency; checkpointing every 10,000 steps risks wasting hours of compute. Design an adaptive interval policy.
day-57-act-03.exercise_prompt: Write a training loop with a registered SIGTERM handler. Launch it, send a kill -15 (SIGTERM) from another shell or process, and verify that the script immediately completes the current step, flushes an emergency checkpoint, and exits cleanly.
day-57-act-03.hint: Use signal.signal(signal.SIGTERM, handler) and flag a boolean to exit after saving checkpoint.
day-57-act-03.answer:
import signal, sys
interrupted = False
def handle_sigterm(signum, frame):
    global interrupted
    print('Received SIGTERM! Preemption impending. Triggering emergency checkpoint...')
    interrupted = True
signal.signal(signal.SIGTERM, handle_sigterm)
# In training loop:
if interrupted:
    save_checkpoint_atomic(payload, 'emergency_ckpt.pt')
    sys.exit(0)
day-57-act-03.mastery_criterion: Trap SIGTERM signals and cleanly save an emergency checkpoint before process exit.

day-57-act-04.title: Assessment: Preemption & Corruption Fault Injection Simulation Drill
day-57-act-04.objective: Execute a full chaotic fault-injection simulation: induce unexpected SIGTERM kills, inject bit corruption into checkpoint files, and verify autonomous self-healing recovery.
day-57-act-04.instructions:
1. Write a supervisor simulation script that runs a 30-step training job.
2. At step 10, inject a simulated SIGTERM. Verify an emergency checkpoint is cleanly saved.
3. At step 20, corrupt the most recent checkpoint file by overwriting the last 512 bytes with zeroes.
4. Relaunch the training runner. Verify that it detects the corruption at step 20, safely falls back to the previous snapshot, and completes all 30 steps with a decreasing loss curve.
day-57-act-04.exercise_prompt: Run the automated chaos drill test suite. Verify that the self-healing training agent logs all anomalies, discards bad checkpoints, and successfully produces the final trained model.
day-57-act-04.hint: Combine safe_load_checkpoint fallback logic with the atomic SIGTERM signal handler.
day-57-act-04.answer:
assert recovered_step >= 10
assert final_step == 30
assert final_loss < initial_loss
day-57-act-04.mastery_criterion: Achieve 100% test pass rate across combined hardware crash and storage corruption drills.
